Subject: SurfaceFlow peak/tail profile + baseline SLOs for Dedicated

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We did a quick internal sizing pass and want to confirm the approach for a dedicated SKU commitment. High level:
- Expected steady-state: 450k tokens/day (~5 TPS average during business hours)
- Peak short spikes: up to 120 TPS sustained for 10-15 minutes (customer-facing feature peak)
- Tail latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens), p99 <= 800ms

Can you confirm whether those peaks map to a single slab or require a multi-slab canary (burst island) under Redwood Dedicated? Also any roughs on the GPU slab sizing (e.g., token/sec per GPU for our usage profile, with KV cache warm vs cold)?

I'll attach the CSV we used to derive token volumes.

—Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Product, SurfaceFlow

Thanks Alex — this is helpful. Looping in Kim (capacity/provisioning) and Ben (solutions ops) to give a concrete slab proposal and a minimal entitlement lane for the initial commit.

Immediate ask: could you confirm the prompt size distribution you expect (median prompt length, fraction >512 tokens)? That matters for token/sec and KV cache hit assumptions. If you don't have that broken down, we'll run a couple of quick assumptions but we'd rather use yours.

High level we tend to model three contributors to capacity: sustained baseline throughput, burst lane (short-duration TPS peaks), and cold-KV start pressure (which increases latency and effective GPU usage). We'll produce a compute sheet and an ops playbook (canary config + fallback to a smaller model) by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: SurfaceFlow — initial slab & headroom calc (attached)

Alex/Tessa —

Attached: surfaceflow_tps_model.xlsx (baseline + three burst scenarios + KV warm/cold assumptions). Summary below.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Prompt distribution: median 64 tokens, 90th pct 320 tokens, 5% >512 tokens (per your note: mostly short).
- Model: open-variant xL-1.3B quantized to int8 profile (we recommend int8 perf + quality check).
- Throughput per A100-like GPU (our benchmark for this model & median length): ~55 tokens/sec sustained with KV warm. Cold-KV effective throughput ~35 tokens/sec during warm-up windows.

Sizing recommendation (initial commit + burst lane):
- Baseline commit: 8 GPUs (handles ~8 * 55 = 440 TPS tokens/sec? NOTE: unit mismatch — we model user TPS as requests/sec and tokens/sec combined; see mapping below).
- Burst island: 2 GPUs reserved as burst capacity to absorb short 10–15 min spikes (holds extra ~110 tokens/sec effective).
- Effective headroom: with autoscaling buffer and KV prewarm, target operational cushion ~20% over modeled peak to keep p95 below 300ms.

Mapping notes (we included the mapping table in the sheet):
- We convert your 120 TPS spike (requests/sec) into tokens/sec by multiplying by average response tokens (we used 120 * 128 = 15,360 tokens/sec as worst-case for spikes) — that drives GPU count.
- For cost/predictability we propose a hybrid: 8 committed GPUs + 2 reserved burst GPUs + policy that routes >80% traffic to committed slab and offloads heavy long-context requests to a lower-cost variant during peak.

Open items / risks:
1) If your long-tail ( >512 tokens) > 10% we need to add 2–4 GPUs to maintain p99.
2) Cold-KV spikes can momentarily raise latency; recommend KV prewarm for scheduled heavy events.
3) Quantization may slightly increase token/sec but requires an eval against your prompts — ask for a small eval set.

I'll be on the call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet.

—Kim Park
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Dedicated

Thanks all — we can pull a 48-hour anonymized trace and Priya will drop it into the shared Drive link (see your related_links). Procurement is looped for the burst amendment and will review the SLA redlines.

Two quick clarifications for Kim:
1) When you say \"55 tokens/sec per GPU\" is that per A100xGPU of a baseline 80-token response or normalized to tokens/sec independent of request shape? We want to be precise for our internal financial model.
2) For the hybrid routing: curious how seamless the automatic fallback is during a multi-minute sustained spike — will customers see model-switching artifacts, or is the plan to keep the same model but route long-context elsewhere?

Appreciate the pragmatic approach — we'll get the traces to you by EOD Friday.

—Alex
